title: Tri-axis eval scratch (verbosity, faithfulness, slotting)
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for a tiny ad-hoc rubric I used this morning while triaging the odd verbose samples we started seeing after the v0.9.3 kernel/quant change. Want something lightweight we can run locally and ship as a tiny smoke test for Dedicated rollouts.

The rubric (tri-axis, scores 0-3):
 - Verbosity: 0 = refuses / empty / single token; 1 = too terse / missing detail; 2 = appropriate length; 3 = long-winded / repetitive.
 - Faithfulness: 0 = hallucination, confidently wrong; 1 = partly wrong/ambiguous; 2 = correct with minor caveats; 3 = perfectly factual and well-cited.
 - Slotting (structure/format): 0 = missing required fields / format broken; 1 = wrong ordering or incomplete; 2 = correct but awkward; 3 = cleanly structured / follows schema.

Scoring notes: keep it fast (one pass), pick a representative prompt per workload (help-center Q/A, code transform, system instruction). Record seed + model + prompt id.

Quick samples (baseline = v0.9.2-prod, current = v0.9.3-quant):

1) Prompt id: HELP-Q-033 (user asks: how to reset API key)
 - baseline (v0.9.2): "Go to Console > API keys, click rotate... short steps + link"
   - Verbosity 2, Faithfulness 2, Slotting 3
 - current (v0.9.3-quant): "You should rotate keys regularly. First find the API keys page, then click rotate button. You might also want to update any SDK instances and check logs to ensure no downtime; if you have a service account, tie the key to it, etc. In general, best practice: rotate every 90 days and audit usage..."
   - Verbosity 3 (rambling), Faithfulness 2 (correct but adds non-specific recommendations), Slotting 3
 - Observation: extra filler sentences inserted — tokens up ~+27% for this prompt. Not strictly wrong but noisier.

2) Prompt id: CODE-REF-211 (transform JS snippet to TS)
 - baseline: concise transformation, preserves types, minimal comments. Scores 2/2/3.
 - current: repeats same transformation but also inserts an explanatory paragraph and a usage example that references an internal repo name ("repo-x/main") which doesn't exist in the prompt context. Scores 1/1/2.
 - Observation: hallucinated repo reference (faithfulness regression), plus verbosity. Appears in 4/20 samples for code prompts.

3) Prompt id: SYS-INSTR-045 (multi-step constraint: return JSON with fields id/title/summary)
 - baseline: returns valid JSON object, all fields present. Scores 2/3/3.
 - current: returns valid JSON but adds additional "meta" field with nested description text and sometimes uses single quotes -> downstream parsers crash. Scores 2/2/1.
 - Observation: slotting regression (formatting), possibly due to tokenizer differences with quotes.

Hypotheses (what changed in v0.9.3-quant that could explain):
 - Quantization path slightly changed attention scaling -> affects repetition/velocity of token generation (verbosity spike).
 - Minor token ID remap (rare) causing apostrophe vs quote preference (slotting).
 - Temperature or sampling fallback altered in runtime when cached KV reused across requests (faithfulness drift).

Quick metrics (back-of-envelope from 50-sample mini-batch):
 - Average tokens per sample: baseline 42 -> current 54 (+28%).
 - Hallucination flagged by heuristics: baseline 6% -> current 18%.
 - JSON parse errors (downstream): baseline 1/50 -> current 6/50.

Immediate actionable next steps (small, do-not-block rollout unless confirmed bad):
 - Add 25 canonical prompts (cover help, code, system) to a guarded smoke test. (TODO: create GH gist with examples)
 - Add a small regex-based JSON validator to parser path to catch slotting regressions early.
 - Reproduce locally with v0.9.2 and v0.9.3-quant and attach top-5 divergent tokens/logs (instrument token-level traces). Ticket: JIRA-ML-472 (assigned to Ravi).
 - If hallucination regression > X% on smoke set, roll back quantization change and do bisect on kernel commits (owner: Lina).

Notes to self / freeform thoughts:
 - This is noisy but not catastrophic — many of the verbose additions are user-visible but not harmful; the real issue is when output invents internal names or breaks machine-parsable outputs.
 - Consider ad-hoc weight on faithfulness > verbosity for safety-critical workloads. For help-center content we may prefer brevity+faithfulness. For creative tasks verbosity is OK.
 - Could add a tiny per-route policy that clips outputs after N sentences for low-latency endpoints. That would hide verbosity regressions but not hallucinations.

Slack snippets (copy-paste):
 - "Heads up QA: seeing increased verbosity and some hallucinated repo refs after v0.9.3-quant. Running a 25-prompt smoke set now. Tagging @ravi for traces."

Todo checklist (short):
 - [ ] Create smoke-set gist + add to ci/smoke-tests (small PR)
 - [ ] Add JSON validator to parsing step (quick Regex)
 - [ ] Run token-trace with seed=42 for 30 samples (Ravi)
 - [ ] If repro, open revert PR for quant commit (Lina)

References/links:
 - JIRA-ML-472 (regression triage)
 - PR GH-PR-8891 (quant path change)
 - local script: ~/evals/tri_axis/run_smoke.py (not checked in yet)

Random quick ideas to try before rolling back:
 - Try forcing greedy sampling for the smoke-set (see if sampling fallback is the problem).
 - Run tokenization diff between v0.9.2 and v0.9.3 with the problematic prompts.
 - Lower top_p temporarily for code endpoints.

Final: save this as a short-lived scratch doc; once smoke set is live, migrate results to confluence/tri-axis-eval and close this draft.

- Clara (quick notes, 2am coffee)
